name: Solutions Chemistry
tagline: Solubility, colligative properties, and solution-phase equilibria.
seo_title: Solutions Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Solutions Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in solubility, solvents, electrolytes, osmosis and colloids.

definition.lead: Solutions chemistry studies what happens when one substance dissolves in another: solubility, concentration and the new properties the mixture gains.
definition.body: Most chemistry, and all of biology, happens in solution. Why salt dissolves in water but not in oil, why seawater freezes below 0 °C and how cells keep their shape all come down to the interactions between solvent and solute.

facts.label: the oldest rule of solubility, still useful today
freezing-point drop per mole of particles in 1 kg of water
Arrhenius proposes that salts split into ions in water

branches.name: Solubility
branches.summary: How much of a substance can dissolve, and what controls it.

branches.name: Colligative properties
branches.summary: Properties that depend only on the number of dissolved particles.
branches.example: Road salt lowers the freezing point of water.

branches.name: Electrolytes & ions
branches.summary: How charged particles behave in solution.

branches.name: Acid–base equilibria
branches.summary: Proton transfer and pH in solution.

branches.name: Solvents & solvation
branches.summary: How solvent molecules surround and stabilize solutes.
branches.example: Replacing toxic solvents with greener ones.

branches.name: Osmosis
branches.summary: Solvent flow through membranes toward higher concentration.
branches.example: Reverse osmosis turns seawater into drinking water.

branches.name: Colloids & micelles
branches.summary: Particles and assemblies suspended in a liquid.

branches.name: Complexation
branches.summary: Metal ions binding ligands in solution.
branches.example: EDTA softens water by binding calcium.

timeline.title: Henry's law
timeline.text: William Henry finds that gas solubility is proportional to its pressure.

timeline.title: Osmotic pressure measured
timeline.text: Wilhelm Pfeffer measures osmotic pressure with semipermeable membranes.
timeline.why: Gave the data that van 't Hoff would explain.

timeline.title: Van 't Hoff's osmotic law
timeline.text: Van 't Hoff shows that dilute solutions behave like gases: πV = nRT.
timeline.why: Unified osmosis with the gas laws.

timeline.title: Ions in solution
timeline.text: Svante Arrhenius proposes that salts dissociate into ions in water.

timeline.title: Ostwald's dilution law
timeline.text: Wilhelm Ostwald links the dissociation of weak acids to dilution.

timeline.title: The pH scale
timeline.why: Acidity of any solution in one number.

timeline.title: Debye–Hückel theory
timeline.text: Peter Debye and Erich Hückel model how ions screen each other.
timeline.why: Explained why real ionic solutions deviate from ideal behaviour.

timeline.title: Practical reverse osmosis
timeline.text: Sidney Loeb and Srinivasa Sourirajan develop a high-flow membrane for desalination.

timeline.title: Crown ethers
timeline.text: Charles Pedersen discovers crown ethers that wrap around metal ions.
timeline.why: Salts could be dissolved in organic solvents; Nobel Prize in 1987.

quiz.q: Why does salt dissolve in water but not in hexane?
options: Salt reacts with water to make new compounds
quiz.explain: Water's partial charges surround each ion (hydration); hexane has no such charges.

quiz.q: Which of these is a colligative property?
quiz.explain: It depends only on how many particles are dissolved, not what they are.

quiz.q: 1 mol of NaCl dissolved in 1 kg of water gives about how many moles of particles?
quiz.explain: Each NaCl gives one Na⁺ and one Cl⁻.

quiz.q: Henry's law: a gas's solubility is proportional to…
options: Its partial pressure above the liquid
quiz.explain: That is why carbonated drinks are bottled under pressure.

quiz.q: Why does a warm soda go flat faster?
options: Gases are less soluble at higher temperature
CO₂ reacts with sugar at higher temperature
quiz.explain: Warming drives dissolved CO₂ out of solution.

quiz.q: In osmosis, water moves across a semipermeable membrane toward…
quiz.explain: Water moves to dilute the side with more dissolved particles.

options: A weak acid and its conjugate base
A strong acid and a strong base
quiz.explain: The pair absorbs added acid or base with little change in pH.

options: Moles of solute per litre of solution
quiz.explain: Moles per kilogram of solvent is molality.

options: Pushing water through a membrane against the osmotic pressure
Boiling the water and condensing the steam
Adding more salt so it settles out
Freezing the water to leave salt behind
quiz.explain: Pressure above the osmotic pressure forces water out and leaves salt behind.

quiz.q: The Ksp of a salt is…
options: The equilibrium constant for dissolving it
Its molar mass in grams per mole
The pH of its saturated solution
Its density in the solid state
quiz.explain: A small Ksp means a poorly soluble salt.
